purpose: Reusable technology-integration axes, validated information-control packages, Power/Reactor candidate/control pairing, and coverage policy for sequential TL design without rebuilding a bespoke stochastic harness for each checkpoint.

pairingPolicy.note: Candidate/control variants should share random streams whenever the changed dimension permits a clean paired comparison.

activationPolicy: Activate only the smallest dependency-relevant submatrix needed to answer the checkpoint question.
Include mixed-TL and high-power-demand contexts whenever a new component can change power, reach, EW, targeting, or defense opportunity cost.
Use actual-consumer preflight plus one-trial full-pipeline smoke before substantive Monte Carlo for any new or materially changed integrated study.

Audit dispatch, pre-run validation, all shared/global release-gate classifications, study-family whitelists, study-specific gates, report routing, schema/baseline bindings, and checkpoint stage definitions before handoff.
Keep outcome/balance targets review-only unless the checkpoint explicitly promotes a deterministic invariant; never make one-trial smoke depend on statistical outcomes.

When Power/Reactor is the changed dependency, pair reactor candidates at identical combat, information-control, and doctrine settings; treat power output, efficiency, condition mapping, overload, and Space as separate axes unless the checkpoint explicitly changes more than one.

currentCoverage.currentExpansion: Power / Reactor is now a first-class axis. CP83 pairs 5 TP vs 6 TP across the same four information-control environments and 12 combat/geometry contexts while holding the validated TL2 information-control working package constant.
currentCoverage.nextExpansion: After CP83 review, promote/revise only the Power/Reactor candidate supported by evidence, then extend the suite along the next dependency-relevant TL2 subsystem axis.
